# Preview fidelity

**Generated by `npm test` — do not edit by hand.**

The live preview and the storefront are two renderers that are *meant* to
differ in markup. What they must agree on is behaviour, so this compares
**numbers**, never markup.

**What is measured:** every price the storefront publishes in its own
rendered output, evaluated through the same evaluator the preview runs, and
checked against the amount that was authored. All three must line up.

**What is measured elsewhere:** that the preview *produces* those published
prices — the authoring tree is converted by `previewTree()`, and its own
suite prices straight off that tree. And that each type draws the right
**control**, which a comparison of numbers cannot see.

## Every option type

| Type | Fidelity | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `radio` | exact (1/1) | Every published price evaluates to the amount the storefront charges. |
| `dropdown` | exact (1/1) | Every published price evaluates to the amount the storefront charges. |
| `checkbox` | exact (1/1) | Every published price evaluates to the amount the storefront charges. |
| `color_swatch` | exact (1/1) | Every published price evaluates to the amount the storefront charges. |
| `image_swatch` | exact (1/1) | Every published price evaluates to the amount the storefront charges. |
| `text_field` | exact | Priced at the option level (per_char) rather than per value, so no per-value price is published. |
| `textarea` | exact | Priced at the option level (per_char) rather than per value, so no per-value price is published. |
| `number_field` | exact | Priced at the option level (per_unit, tiered) rather than per value, so no per-value price is published. |
| `range` | exact | Priced at the option level (per_unit, tiered) rather than per value, so no per-value price is published. |
| `quantity` | exact | Priced at the option level (per_unit, tiered) rather than per value, so no per-value price is published. |
| `date_picker` | exact | Carries no price of its own, so there is nothing to compare. |
| `time_picker` | exact | Carries no price of its own, so there is nothing to compare. |
| `datetime_picker` | exact | Carries no price of its own, so there is nothing to compare. |
| `hidden` | not previewed | The customer supplies no answer here, so there is nothing to price. |
| `file_input` | not previewed | The customer supplies no answer here, so there is nothing to price. |

*`exact` means every published price evaluates to the amount the storefront
charges. `not previewed` means the customer supplies no answer to price.*

## Recorded limits

These are deliberate, each with a decision behind it.

| Limit | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Pricing shown** | The preview prices what the **server** charges — all five price types. The storefront’s own live estimate shows `fixed` only, because *“a storefront guessing… would show a total the server disagrees with.”* (ADR-107) |
| **Column counts** | `columns` is a **maximum, not a count**. The storefront gives every count one `auto-fit` rule with a `7em` minimum, so the number decides whether a grid applies, never how many columns appear. (ADR-108) |
| **Collapsed groups** | `collapsed_by_default` de-emphasises rather than collapses, on both sides. Honouring it in CSS alone *“would hide a control from sighted customers while leaving it in the tab order.”* |
| **Preview width** | The three presets are **viewport** widths, but the frame is a content column — narrower in any real theme. There is no way to know a theme’s column width, which is why the storefront owns none. (ADR-108) |
| **Base price** | A real product’s price is a **mirror of the last catalogue push**, not a live quote: `StoreProduct` is display-only, and the catalogue is push-driven. (ADR-067, ADR-101) |
| **Multiple sets** | The preview prices **one set**. A product may carry several, and the storefront sums every one into a single line total. |
| **Selection and date bounds** | `min_selections`, `max_selections`, `min_date` and `max_date` are **server-enforced only** — no template sends them to a browser, so the preview sends none either. |
| **Control shape** | The table above reads **numbers, never markup** (ADR-109), so it cannot see a control drawn wrongly. Control shape is pinned separately, against this same fixture. |
| **Unordered entries** | An option or heading with **no** `sort_order` sorts *first* in the preview and *last* on the storefront, which defaults it to `PHP_INT_MAX` so that *“a document missing `sort_order`”* cannot hoist itself above everything the merchant did order. Unreachable through the API — `sortOrder` is required and defaults to `0` — so the preview does not add a branch no data can take. |
| **Dialect safety** | The authoring and published shapes are both `Record<string, unknown>`, so reading an authoring key off a converted value **compiles**. The seam is held by tests and ADR-103, never by the compiler; a branded type cannot help, because an intersection is still assignable to the converter’s parameter. |
